title: What is RPL? A plain-English guide for Australians
metaTitle: What is RPL? Recognition of Prior Learning Explained
metaDescription: What Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) is, who it suits, how the assessment works and what you get at the end. A plain-English guide for Australians.
excerpt: RPL turns the skills you already have into a nationally recognised qualification. Here's what it means, who it suits and how the assessment works.
imageAlt: Two construction workers in hi-vis vests reviewing building plans on a table

faqs.q: What does RPL stand for?
faqs.a: RPL stands for Recognition of Prior Learning. It is the formal process registered training organisations use to assess skills you gained through work and life experience, and award the matching units of a nationally recognised qualification.

faqs.q: Is an RPL certificate real?
faqs.a: Yes. A qualification gained through RPL is the same nationally recognised qualification, with the same code and title, as one gained by studying. It is issued by a registered training organisation and recorded against your Unique Student Identifier.

faqs.q: Does my certificate say it was done by RPL?
faqs.a: The certificate (testamur) is the same as for any other student. Your record of results may show that units were granted through RPL, which is how the national system records the way each unit was achieved.

faqs.q: How much experience do I need for RPL?
faqs.a: It depends on the qualification. As a rough guide, people who have done the work for a few years are usually good candidates. Higher qualifications and licensed trades generally need more, and broader, experience. A free eligibility check will tell you where you stand.

faqs.q: Can I do RPL if my experience is from overseas?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Overseas experience can count if you can show it with evidence such as references, photos and documents, and explain how your work meets Australian standards. Some trades also need a separate skills assessment or licence.

title: How to get RPL in Australia: step by step
metaTitle: How to Get RPL in Australia: Step-by-Step Guide
metaDescription: The seven steps to a qualification through RPL in Australia: eligibility, choosing a qualification, your USI, evidence, assessment, gaps and your certificate.
excerpt: From the eligibility check to your certificate in the mail: the seven steps of an RPL assessment, what to expect at each one, and the mistakes that slow people down.
imageAlt: Tradesperson with a tool belt working on a timber wall frame

faqs.q: How do I get an RPL certificate in Australia?
faqs.a: Choose the qualification that matches your experience, enrol with a registered training organisation, collect evidence of your skills, and complete the assessment, which usually includes a competency conversation. If you are competent in every unit, the RTO issues your qualification.

faqs.q: Do I need a USI for RPL?
faqs.a: Yes. You need a Unique Student Identifier to be issued any nationally recognised qualification, including through RPL. It is free and takes a few minutes to create on the government's USI website.

faqs.q: What is a competency conversation?
faqs.a: It is a structured interview with your assessor, often by video call, about how you do your job. You explain the tasks, how you solve problems and how you follow safety and quality rules, using real examples from your work.

faqs.q: What happens if I don't have enough evidence?
faqs.a: The assessor tells you which units have gaps. You can usually close them with extra evidence, such as another reference or more photos, or with short gap training for those units only.

faqs.q: Can I choose which qualification to apply for?
faqs.a: Yes, but it should match the work you actually do, at the level you do it. Choosing a qualification that is too high leads to gaps; choosing one that is too low undersells your experience.

title: How much does RPL cost? What affects the price
metaTitle: RPL Cost in Australia: What Affects the Price
metaDescription: What drives the cost of RPL in Australia: qualification size, trade assessments, gap training and funding. What a quote should include and cheap-RPL red flags.
excerpt: There's no single national price for RPL. Here's what drives the cost, what a fair quote should include, where funding can help, and the warning signs of a too-cheap offer.
imageAlt: Person using a calculator next to a laptop on a wooden desk

faqs.q: Why don't you list RPL prices?
faqs.a: Because the price depends on your experience, the qualification and the registered training organisation that assesses you. A free eligibility check lets us give you an accurate quote rather than a misleading starting price.

faqs.q: Is RPL cheaper than doing the course?
faqs.a: For experienced workers it usually costs less overall, mainly because you don't take time off work or pay to learn skills you already have. If you are new to the industry, a course may be better value because RPL would leave large gaps.

faqs.q: Can I pay for RPL in instalments?
faqs.a: Many providers offer payment plans. Ask for the plan details in writing as part of your quote, including any fees for paying in instalments.

faqs.q: Is there government funding for RPL?
faqs.a: Some state-funded training programs cover RPL for eligible people at participating providers. Eligibility depends on the state, the qualification and your circumstances, such as residency and qualifications you already hold.

faqs.q: Is RPL tax-deductible?
faqs.a: Work-related self-education costs can be deductible in some situations, for example when the qualification relates to your current job. It depends on your circumstances, so check with the ATO or a registered tax agent.

title: Getting your electrical licence through RPL
metaTitle: Electrical Licence Through RPL: State-by-State Guide
metaDescription: How RPL works for UEE30820 Cert III in Electrotechnology Electrician, who it suits, the capstone, and which regulator licenses electricians in each state.
excerpt: RPL can get you the UEE30820 qualification an electrical licence needs, but the licence comes from your state's regulator. Here's how the pathway works and who it suits.
imageAlt: Electrician in a hard hat working on a wall socket

faqs.q: Can I become a licensed electrician through RPL?
faqs.a: RPL can get you the UEE30820 Certificate III in Electrotechnology Electrician if you have substantial, supervised electrical experience. The licence itself is issued by your state or territory regulator, which may have extra requirements such as a capstone or its own assessment.

faqs.q: Can electrical RPL be done fully online?
faqs.a: Usually not entirely. Your evidence and competency conversation can often be done remotely, but the practical and capstone assessments generally need to be completed in person under observation.

faqs.q: What is the capstone assessment?
faqs.a: It is a final practical and theory assessment in the electrician qualification that checks you can install, test and verify electrical work safely and to standard. Victoria also requires Energy Safe Victoria's Licensed Electrician's Assessment (LEA).

faqs.q: I'm an electrician from overseas. What do I need?
faqs.a: Usually an Australian skills assessment and an Australian licence. Many states issue a provisional or restricted licence first, so you can work under supervision while completing requirements such as gap training and the capstone.

faqs.q: Can I work in another state with my electrical licence?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Electrical licences can generally be recognised in other states through mutual recognition, and some jurisdictions recognise each other's licences automatically. Check the rules of the state you want to work in.

title: Plumbing licence through RPL: Cert III vs Cert IV explained
metaTitle: Plumbing Licence RPL: Cert III vs Cert IV Explained
metaDescription: CPC32420 Cert III in Plumbing vs CPC40920 Cert IV in Plumbing and Services: how RPL works for each, and which regulator licenses plumbers in your state.
excerpt: The Cert III makes you a plumber; the Cert IV is usually what lets you hold a full licence and take responsibility for the work. Here's how RPL works for each.
imageAlt: Stack of PVC plumbing pipes seen end-on

faqs.q: Do I need a Cert IV to get a plumbing licence?
faqs.a: In many states, the Certificate IV in Plumbing and Services (CPC40920), or specific units from it, is required for a full licence, to certify work or to contract. The exact rules depend on your state's regulator and the licence class you want.

faqs.q: Can I get the Cert IV in Plumbing through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are a qualified plumber with experience after your trade in the areas the units cover, such as design, sizing, compliance and supervision. Choose electives that match the licence classes you need.

faqs.q: How long does plumbing RPL take?
faqs.a: Usually weeks, depending mostly on how quickly you collect evidence and references. A practical assessment, if needed, can add a little time.

faqs.q: Is a plumbing licence from one state valid in another?
faqs.a: Plumbing licences can often be recognised in other states through mutual recognition arrangements, but licence classes differ. Check with the regulator in the state where you want to work.

title: Can you do RPL online?
metaTitle: Can You Do RPL Online? How Online RPL Works
metaDescription: Yes, most RPL can be done online. How it works, which qualifications need an in-person practical, video evidence tips and how to spot a provider to avoid.
excerpt: Most RPL can be done entirely online: upload your evidence, talk to an assessor by video call and get your qualification without a classroom. Here's how it works.
imageAlt: Person typing on a laptop at a wooden table

faqs.q: Is an online RPL qualification recognised?
faqs.a: Yes. If a registered training organisation assessed you properly, the qualification is the same nationally recognised qualification whether the assessment happened online or in person.

faqs.q: How is the competency conversation done online?
faqs.a: By video call with your assessor. You need a device with a camera and microphone, a stable internet connection and a quiet place to talk for the length of the session.

faqs.q: Can I do RPL online from a regional area?
faqs.a: Yes. Online RPL works anywhere in Australia with an internet connection, which is why it is popular with regional, remote and FIFO workers.

faqs.q: Which qualifications can't be done fully online?
faqs.a: Qualifications that lead to licences or need safety-critical skills shown live, such as electrical work or CPR, usually include an in-person practical. Everything else in the assessment can still be done online.

title: Evidence for RPL: what to collect and how
metaTitle: RPL Evidence: What to Collect and How to Present It
metaDescription: What counts as RPL evidence: references, photos, videos, work documents and tickets. What assessors look for, what to collect and how to organise it.
excerpt: Good evidence is the fastest way through RPL. Here's what assessors look for, what to collect for trades, care and office roles, and how to organise it so nothing gets missed.
imageAlt: Two red ring-binder folders standing on a desk

faqs.q: What are the four rules of evidence?
faqs.a: Assessors check that evidence is valid (relevant to the unit), sufficient (enough of it), authentic (your own work) and current (recent enough to reflect how the job is done today).

faqs.q: Are payslips good evidence for RPL?
faqs.a: Only as support. Payslips show you were employed but not what you can do. Combine them with evidence of the actual tasks, such as photos, work documents and supervisor reports.

faqs.q: Who should write my RPL reference?
faqs.a: Someone who saw your work directly, such as a supervisor, manager or long-term client. The reference should describe the tasks you did, for how long and to what standard, with their contact details.

faqs.q: What if my old employer has closed down?
faqs.a: Use other sources: former supervisors or colleagues, clients, photos, documents you kept and your own detailed statement. The assessor may also ask for a practical demonstration to confirm your skills.

faqs.q: Do I need all my evidence before I start?
faqs.a: No. Start with what you have. An eligibility check will show which qualification it supports and what is still missing, so you can collect the rest with a clear target.

title: RPL vs apprenticeship vs TAFE: which path fits you?
metaTitle: RPL vs Apprenticeship vs TAFE: Which Path Fits You?
metaDescription: RPL, an apprenticeship and TAFE can lead to the same qualification. Compare time, income and who each pathway suits, with examples for common situations.
excerpt: All three can lead to the same qualification. The difference is how you get there, and the right choice depends mostly on how much experience you already have.
imageAlt: Tradesperson's hands working at a bench covered in hand tools

faqs.q: Is RPL as good as an apprenticeship?
faqs.a: The qualification is identical. An apprenticeship is the right path if you are new to a trade; RPL is for people who already have the skills and need them formally recognised.

faqs.q: Can I use RPL to finish an apprenticeship I didn't complete?
faqs.a: Often, yes. RPL can recognise the units you have already done on the job, so you only train for what is left. Talk to a registered training organisation about your training records.

faqs.q: Does TAFE offer RPL?
faqs.a: Yes. Many TAFE institutes and private registered training organisations offer RPL. RPL is a method of assessment, not a type of provider.

faqs.q: Which is fastest: RPL, apprenticeship or TAFE?
faqs.a: For an experienced worker, RPL is usually fastest, typically taking weeks. Apprenticeships usually take three to four years, and TAFE courses take months to a couple of years.

title: Using overseas work experience for RPL in Australia
metaTitle: Overseas Work Experience for RPL in Australia
metaDescription: Can overseas experience count for RPL? What evidence to use, how translations work and what RPL can't do for a visa. A plain-English guide.
excerpt: Yes, experience from overseas can count towards RPL. Here's the evidence to gather, how translations work and what RPL can't replace.

faqs.q: Does overseas work experience count for RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if it is relevant to the qualification and you can prove it. Assessors look at what you can do and whether your evidence is valid, sufficient, authentic and current, not where you gained the experience.

faqs.q: Do my documents need to be translated?
faqs.a: Documents not in English usually need an English translation. Some training organisations accept a professional translation and others require a certified one, so ask before you pay.

faqs.q: Can I get a licence in Australia using overseas experience and RPL?
faqs.a: A qualification can be a step towards a licence, but licences are issued by state regulators who set their own requirements. Check with the regulator for your trade.

faqs.q: Is RPL the same as a skills assessment for a visa?
faqs.a: No. A skills assessment for migration is done by the assessing authority for your occupation. RPL with a training organisation is separate, so check visa requirements with a registered migration agent.

title: Becoming a trainer and assessor: TAE40122 through RPL
metaTitle: TAE40122 Through RPL: Trainer & Assessor Guide
metaDescription: How to get the TAE40122 Certificate IV in Training and Assessment through RPL: who qualifies, what evidence you need and how assessment works.
excerpt: If you already train or assess people at work, you may be able to get the TAE40122 through RPL. Here's who qualifies and what evidence to collect.

faqs.q: Can I get the TAE40122 through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you already design, deliver or assess training and can show it with evidence such as session plans, recordings and assessment records.

faqs.q: Do I need to deliver a session for RPL?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The qualification includes practical delivery and assessment, so expect to deliver or assess a live or recorded session.

faqs.q: Can I teach a trade with only the TAE40122?
faqs.a: No. You also need the vocational competence and current industry skills for what you teach, usually shown by holding the qualification you deliver.

faqs.q: Is the TAE40122 the current qualification?
faqs.a: Yes. It replaced the TAE40116, and RTOs are expected to use the current version.

title: Security licence and RPL: what to check in your state
metaTitle: Security Licence & RPL: What to Check First
metaDescription: Security licences are issued by state regulators and some restrict RPL. Learn how qualifications and licences differ and what to confirm first.
excerpt: A security licence comes from your state regulator, and some limit RPL. Here's how qualifications and licences fit together and what to check first.

faqs.q: Does a security qualification give me a licence?
faqs.a: No. Qualifications come from a registered training organisation and licences come from your state or territory regulator, which has its own requirements.

faqs.q: Can I use RPL for security licence training?
faqs.a: It depends on the state and the licence class. Some regulators restrict RPL, so confirm with the regulator or us before you enrol.

faqs.q: What evidence can security officers use for RPL?
faqs.a: A current or previous licence, a statement of service, de-identified incident reports and patrol logs, and first aid certificates. Supervisors can add rosters and risk assessments.

faqs.q: Which qualification do I need for a master security licence?
faqs.a: Some states require a management-level qualification such as the Certificate IV in Security and Management. Requirements differ, so check your regulator.

title: RPL for aged care, disability and community services workers
metaTitle: RPL for Aged Care & Community Services Workers
metaDescription: Turn care work experience into a Certificate III or higher through RPL. Qualifications, evidence and screening checks for community services.
excerpt: Working in aged care, disability, childcare or community services? Here's how RPL can turn that experience into a qualification.

faqs.q: Can I get a Certificate III in Individual Support through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have worked in aged care, disability or home care and can show evidence of your duties, training and workplace skills.

faqs.q: What evidence do care workers need?
faqs.a: A reference or statement of service, position description, training certificates, de-identified shift notes, and any screening checks you hold.

faqs.q: Do I need an NDIS Worker Screening Check?
faqs.a: Workers in risk-assessed roles with NDIS-registered providers need one. It is a screening requirement, separate from your qualification.

faqs.q: Does RPL cover work placement hours?
faqs.a: Often your existing work can cover placement, but the training organisation decides what it accepts. We confirm this at your eligibility check.

title: Mechanic RPL: get your automotive trade certificate
metaTitle: Mechanic RPL: Automotive Trade Certificate Guide
metaDescription: Experienced mechanic with no certificate? Learn how RPL can give you a Certificate III or IV in automotive, what evidence to use and state licensing.
excerpt: Worked as a mechanic without a trade certificate? Here's how RPL can recognise your skills with a Certificate III or IV in automotive.

faqs.q: Can I get a mechanic's certificate through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have enough hands-on experience and can show it with photos, job cards and a reference. A practical assessment is usually part of it.

faqs.q: Do I need a licence to work as a mechanic?
faqs.a: Most states do not license individual mechanics, but some regulate repairers. For example NSW and Western Australia have schemes that look for a Certificate III.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate licence for air conditioning?
faqs.a: Handling vehicle air conditioning refrigerant needs an ARC licence, which is separate from your trade qualification.

faqs.q: Can I use overseas trade certificates?
faqs.a: Yes, they can be used as evidence, translated if needed, alongside photos, job cards and a reference.
